newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-SILVERWOOD SHINES BUT ENGLAND STRUGGLE.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-SILVERWOOD SHINES BUT ENGLAND STRUGGLE.

text.p: Fast-medium Chris Silverwood grabbed six wickets on Thursday as England bowled out New Zealand A for 181, but the tourists lost three top batsmen in a faltering reply.
Troubled captain Mike Atherton, fellow opener Nick Knight and John Crawley all fell cheaply as England struggled to 30 for three at the close.

Atherton has been ridiculed and criticised by commentators back home for failing to gain an England victory in this week's first test, where New Zealand's last wicket pair staged a century partnership to draw the match.
Short of runs on tour apart from his second innings 83 in the test, he scored just five on Thursday before being caught off an attempted hook.

New Zealand A new ball pair Geoff Allott and Heath Davis turned in impressive spells to cut through the England top order. Nasser Hussain and Craig White were left with the task of rebuilding the innings on Friday.
Earlier, Silverwood staked a strong claim to a test place by claiming a career-best six for 44.

New Zealand A's prospective test batsmen mostly disappointed, apart from a third wicket stand of 97 between opener Darrin Murray and Matt Horne. Horne top-scored with an aggressive 64 before being bowled by Silverwood.
Andrew Caddick chipped in with two wickets, while Robert Croft and Phil Tufnell claimed one each.
